resources.string: Recovery key
On. Your recovery key ranks above the server's key.
Off. Only the server's key can change your identity.
Checking…
Couldn't check. Open to try again.
Your identity is @%1$s, the name people and apps know you by. %2$s hosts your account and holds the key that can change your identity.
A recovery key is a second key that ranks above %1$s's key. With it, you can replace %1$s's key for @%2$s if that key is lost or you stop trusting it.
Your recovery key comes from your 12-word recovery phrase, so there is nothing new to write down. %1$s only gets the public part of the key, which lets it recognize your key but not use it.

For now, %1$s keeps the only record of your identity, so every change to it, including the ones on this page, goes through %1$s. Undoing a change to your identity isn't available yet. When it is, a change can only be undone within 72 hours of being made.
Anyone with your 12 words can use your recovery key for @%1$s. Store them where only you can get to them.

Turn on recovery key
Save and confirm your recovery phrase first.
Turn on your recovery key?
%1$s will add your recovery key to @%2$s, ranked above its own key. You'll confirm with your passkey first. After that, this device can use your recovery phrase to replace %1$s's key.
Turn on
Status
Recovery key is on
Your recovery key ranks above %1$s's key for @%2$s.
This device's phrase doesn't match
@%1$s has a recovery key made from a different recovery phrase, so this device can't use it. If you still have that phrase, use it on the device that has it.
This device has no recovery phrase
This device can't use your recovery key without the recovery phrase you turned it on with. Use a device that has that phrase.
Lost the other phrase?
Replace the recovery key on @%1$s with one made from this device's recovery phrase. %2$s makes this change with its own key, and you confirm with your passkey.
Save and confirm this device's recovery phrase first.
Replace recovery key
Replace your recovery key?

The recovery key on @%2$s will be replaced with one made from this device's recovery phrase. The old phrase will no longer work for @%2$s. %1$s makes the change with its own key, and you'll confirm with your passkey.
Replace
Done. @%1$s now uses the recovery key from this device's phrase.
Replace the server's key
If %1$s's key for @%2$s is lost, or you think someone else used it, replace it with a new key. Your recovery phrase approves the change on this device, and you confirm with your passkey.
Replace the server's key
Replace the server's key?
Here is what will happen:
This device checks that the change only replaces the server's key, then approves it with your recovery phrase. The phrase never leaves this device.
You confirm with your passkey.
The key %1$s uses for @%2$s stops working, and a new one replaces it.
Your recovery key still ranks above the new key.
Your journal, sign-in methods and devices don't change.
Replace key
Done. %1$s now uses a new key for @%2$s, and the old key can no longer change your identity.
Recovery keys aren't available here. They need a server that supports them and a device that can confirm with a passkey.
